app_tagline: Build the dot diagram, compress it with FA, HA and CPA, and see the circuit you built.
status_error_title: The dotree core failed to load.
wip_notice: Under construction: dotree already builds the matrix, compresses it to a complete circuit, draws the block diagram, verifies the circuit, generates VHDL and offers help on demand; the exercise is saved in this browser and can be exported and opened as a file.
form_expression_hint: Upper-case letters are variables; use +, * (or ×, ·, or adjacent letters) and integer coefficients. E.g. A*B + C*D + 3(E+F) + G
warning_unused_width: The width of {var} was ignored: the expression does not use {var}.
error_syntax_lowercase: Variables are upper-case letters: “{char}” at column {column} should be “{upper}”.
error_syntax_unexpected_end: The expression ended too early (column {column}). Expected: {expected}.
error_syntax_zero: Zero coefficient at column {column}: coefficients start at 1.
error_width_out_of_range: The width of {var} must be between {min} and {max} bits (it is {width}).
error_repeated_variable: {var} appears twice in the same product: powers are out of this version.
error_no_variables: The expression needs at least one variable: constants alone make no circuit.
error_too_many_input_bits: The inputs add up to {total} bits; the limit is {limit}.
error_too_many_dots: The matrix would have {count} dots; the limit is {limit}.
width_question: How many bits does the output R need so that no value of the expression is lost?
width_answer_invalid: Answer with a whole number of bits, from 1 up.
width_confirm_result_body: The app shows W but not the working: that takes a second request.
width_right: Correct! The output has W = {width} bits.
width_wrong: Not this time: you answered {answer}. The output has W = {width} bits.
width_confirm_path_title: See how W is worked out?
width_confirm_path_body: Try first: what is the largest value the expression can take?
width_path_vmax: The largest value of the expression:
width_path_w: W is the fewest bits that hold that value:
reject_mixed_columns: A cell adds bits of the same weight.
reject_wrong_count: An FA takes 3 points; an HA takes 2. The selection has {count}.
reject_already_in_cell: Each point goes into one cell per level.
reject_not_in_current_level: Only points of the current level form cells.
reject_duplicate_selection: The same point was picked twice.
reject_empty_level: A level needs at least one cell.
keyboard_hint: Keyboard: Tab moves through the points, Space selects, F forms the cell, Esc clears the selection, Ctrl+Z undoes, Ctrl+Y redoes, V switches the view.
solution_applied: {method}'s solution applied. Undo brings your circuit back.
cpa_block_column_too_tall: Column 2^{column} has {height} points; the CPA takes at most 3.
cpa_block_three_not_first: Column 2^{column} has 3 points; only the lowest column with 2 or more points may have 3.
cpa_block_nothing_to_add: No column has 2 or more points: there is nothing to add.
cpa_block_pending_cells: There are pending cells: conclude the level before the CPA.
result_column_zero: Column of weight 2^{column}, bit R{column} constant 0
complete: Circuit complete: the result has {width} bits, R0 to R{top}.
dropped_note: The carry of {cells} is always 0 and becomes no point.
dropped_confirm_title: See why this carry is always 0?
dropped_confirm_body: The explanation shows the output width, W.
dropped_explain: The output has W = {width} bits, 2^0 to 2^{top}, because the expression is at most {vmax}. A carry into column 2^{width} would be worth at least 2^{width}, more than that maximum; so it is always 0.
back_confirm_body: The cells of level {level} become pending again, for editing, and those of the later levels are discarded. Undo brings everything back.
discard_confirm_body: Building another matrix erases the compression in progress, and that cannot be undone.
rules_fa: FA: 3 points of the same column become the sum, in the same column, and the carry, in the next column, on the next level. It costs 1 A_FA and 1 T_FA.
rules_ha: HA: the same with 2 points. It costs 0.5 A_FA and 0.5 T_FA.
rules_level: Each point goes into one cell per level; the points left over pass straight to the next level.
rules_cpa: The CPA closes a level where no column has more than 2 points, except the lowest column with 2 or more, which may have 3.
rules_done: The circuit is complete when every column has at most 1 point: those are the result bits.
help_lower_bound_path: See how the bound is reached
confirm_hint_body: The hint talks about the current level, without saying which points to pick.
confirm_next_move_body: The app highlights the points of the cell Dadda's method would form now. Nothing is formed unless you ask.
confirm_lower_bound_body: First only the number; the reasoning comes with a second request.
confirm_lower_bound_path_title: See how the lower bound is reached?
confirm_lower_bound_path_body: First try: how many points does each FA remove? And each HA?
confirm_solution_body: First only the final metrics; the levels come with a second request. Your circuit does not change.
confirm_solution_path_body: First compare the solution's metrics with your circuit's.
confirm_use_solution_body: The circuit you built gives way to {method}'s whole solution. Undo (Ctrl+Z) brings your circuit back.

match.levels=1: With maximum height {height}, at least {levels} level is left before the CPA.
match.levels=*: With maximum height {height}, at least {levels} levels are left before the CPA.

hint_tallest_column: Column 2^{column} is the tallest ({height} points); the CPA takes at most 3 in the first column and 2 in the others.
hint_idle_points: Some points ready at t = 0 are in no cell yet, in a column with 3 or more points.
hint_cpa_ready: This level can already be closed with the CPA.
move_form_cell: Dadda's next move: an {kind} with {points}, in column 2^{column}. The points are highlighted.
move_conclude_level: Dadda's next move: conclude the level.
move_close_with_cpa: Dadda's next move: close with the CPA.
lower_bound_result: Lower bound: {value}. No circuit for this matrix uses fewer than {value} FA plus dropped carries.
lower_bound_path: Points of the initial matrix minus W: {dots} − {width} = {value}. Each FA removes 1 point (3 in, 2 out), each dropped carry removes 1, and the HA removes none (2 in, 2 out). The complete circuit has at most W points, so FA + dropped carries ≥ {dots} − {width}. It is a lower bound, not necessarily the optimum.

match.levels=1: {method}'s solution: {levels} level and the CPA; {fa} FA, {ha} HA; area {area} A_FA; delay {delay} T_FA.
match.levels=*: {method}'s solution: {levels} levels and the CPA; {fa} FA, {ha} HA; area {area} A_FA; delay {delay} T_FA.

match.levels=1: {method}'s solution: {levels} level; {fa} FA, {ha} HA; area {area} A_FA; delay {delay} T_FA.
match.levels=*: {method}'s solution: {levels} levels; {fa} FA, {ha} HA; area {area} A_FA; delay {delay} T_FA.

solution_rule_dadda: Dadda postpones the reduction: at each level, each column only comes down to the target height, the largest number of the sequence 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 13… below the tallest column, with FA, and HA when only 1 is left to reduce.
solution_rule_wallace: Wallace reduces as early as possible: at each level, each column uses every FA its points allow, and an HA only when it would still be over the target height, 2⌊h/3⌋ + (h mod 3) for the tallest height h.
diagram_empty: The diagram appears once a level is concluded.
diagram_incomplete: Incomplete circuit: the diagram goes up to level {level}. Exports become available once the circuit is complete.
comparison_empty: Ask for Dadda's or Wallace's solution to compare it with your circuit. The comparison only shows what you already asked for.
comparison_missing: {method}'s solution comes in here once you ask for its metrics.
comparison_pareto_note: Non-dominated: no other complete solution has area and delay both smaller or equal, with at least one of them smaller. An incomplete circuit is left out.
comparison_dadda_note: Classic Dadda: an HA when only 1 is left to reduce. Parhami's fig. 8.14 draws a variant with as many FA and fewer HA.
verify_cancelled: Verification cancelled; no result was recorded.
verify_failed: Error at case {checked} of {total}: the circuit does not compute the expression. Verification stopped at the first counterexample.
vhdl_name_invalid: Invalid name: start with a letter and use only letters, digits and _ (no __ and no trailing _); do not use a VHDL reserved word or a name the circuit already uses (ports, signals, cells).
vhdl_copy_failed: Could not copy {file}; select the code and copy it by hand.
vhdl_board_ok: Includes the DE2 board top ({file}) and the Quartus project: the variables come from the SW switches, and the result shows on the LEDR LEDs and, in hexadecimal, on the HEX displays.
vhdl_board_too_many_inputs: No DE2 board top: the board has {max} switches, and this circuit has {bits} input bits.
vhdl_board_too_wide: No DE2 board top: the displays show up to {max} bits, and the result has {width}.
file_import_failed: Could not open {file}: {reason} The open exercise did not change.
file_error_too_large: the file is over 1 MB, too large for an exercise.
file_error_not_exercise: {subject} is JSON, but not a dotree exercise.
file_error_old_schema: {subject} uses schema {found}, too old for this version.
file_error_future_schema: {subject} uses schema {found}, from a newer version of dotree.
file_error_bad_expression: the expression or the widths do not build a valid matrix.
file_error_inconsistent_cell: cell {position} of level {level} breaks the compression rules.
file_error_inconsistent_level: level {level} cannot exist at that point of the exercise.
file_error_inconsistent_reveals: the reveal log is impossible (a step 2 without its step 1).
saved_offer: There is an exercise saved in this browser: {expression}.
saved_corrupt: The exercise saved in this browser could not be opened: {reason} Download the saved content before discarding it if you want to keep it.
saved_confirm_body: The exercise saved in this browser will be erased, and that cannot be undone.
storage_unavailable: This browser does not let the page store data: the exercise works normally, but progress will not be remembered when the tab closes. Use “Export exercise” to keep it.
verify_error_load: The verification could not run: the verification module did not load. Reload the page with the network available.
read_only_notice: Narrow screen: below 768 px the exercise is read-only. Matrix, diagram, verification and VHDL stay available; to form cells, use a wider window.
form_profile_hint: Or a height profile: the input heights and, after the semicolon, the output heights, from the most significant column to the least. E.g. {example}
error_profile_syntax: Malformed height profile at column {column}. Use heights separated by commas, a semicolon and the output heights, in braces, as in {example}.
error_profile_no_dots: The profile has no input dot.
error_profile_too_many_dots: The profile has {dots} dots; the limit is {limit}, one per letter from A to Z.
error_profile_too_many_columns: A list of the profile has more than {limit} columns.
error_profile_output_too_small: The output cannot hold the input from column 2^{column} up: dots never move to a lower column.
error_profile_empty_column: The output asks for 0 dots in column 2^{column}, but it will always hold at least one: a column with a dot never empties, since every cell leaves its sum in it.
profile_target: Asked for: {profile}, from the most significant column to the least. The reduction stops when no column is above the height asked for.
profile_reached: Profile reached: area {area} A_FA, delay {delay} T_FA.
profile_over_column: column 2^{column} has {height}, the profile asks for {target}
profile_pending: Conclude the level to check the profile.
profile_block_confirm_title: See the name of the block?
profile_block_confirm_body: Recognising the block is part of the exercise. The name counts as help.
block_adder_carry_in: It is a {bits}-bit adder with carry in.
block_carry_save: It is {bits} FA side by side: a {bits}-bit carry-save adder.
block_counter: It is a generalized parallel counter: the output has one bit per column.
block_compressor: It is a compressor: the output stays in redundant form, with more than one bit in some column.
optimal_ask_path: See the optimal solution level by level
optimal_confirm_path_title: See the optimal solution level by level?
optimal_confirm_use_title: Replace your circuit with the optimal solution?
optimal_confirm_use_body: The circuit you built gives way to the whole optimal solution. Undo (Ctrl+Z) brings your circuit back.
optimal_output: Optimal solution, output in the profile
optimal_rule: The optimal solution comes from a search: among the circuits of FA and HA that reach the profile, the one with the least area and, among those, the least delay. Each cell takes the earliest ready dots of its column.

match.levels=1: Optimal solution: {levels} level; {fa} FA, {ha} HA; area {area} A_FA; delay {delay} T_FA.
match.levels=*: Optimal solution: {levels} levels; {fa} FA, {ha} HA; area {area} A_FA; delay {delay} T_FA.

optimal_applied: Optimal solution applied. Undo brings your circuit back.
optimal_too_large: This profile is too large for the search of the optimal solution: it passed its limit of attempts.
optimal_no_circuit: No circuit of FA and HA reaches this profile.
comparison_missing_optimal: The optimal solution comes in here once you ask for its metrics.
comparison_profile_note: With an output profile, a solution counts as complete when it reaches the profile.
comparison_heights_export_optimal: Download the heights of the optimal solution (Markdown)
